stem:
Indira's family follows a purely lunar calendar. Each month begins with a new Moon, and twelve lunar months make one lunar year of about 354 days. A festival fixed to one lunar month falls in cool weather one year but, after several years, falls in hot weather.

Why does a purely lunar calendar not keep the same months aligned with the same seasons year after year?

options.text: The Moon's phases change randomly, so no lunar calendar can repeat in a regular way.
Twelve lunar months total about 354 days, which is shorter than the roughly 365-day seasonal year, so the lunar year ends earlier and the months drift through the seasons.
The seasons themselves become a little shorter each year, so the lunar months can no longer keep pace with them.
Twelve lunar months total more than 365 days, so the lunar year runs long and the months drift the other way.

teacher.key_rationale: A lunar year of about 354 days is shorter than the seasonal year of about 365 days, so lunar months shift relative to the seasons.
